title: Telemetry Pulse Aggregator and Contextual Paging for Latency Regression Alerts
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Build a telemetry "pulse" aggregator that fuses tracing hooks, metrics and log-derived signals to produce route-aware anomaly scores and burn-rate alerts, and to drive contextual paging decisions (who gets paged, when).

Scope:
- Instrument request paths with a lightweight telemetry-id header and ensure ingestion of span-level timing + selected logs.
- Extend ingest pipeline to produce a 'pulse_score' per (service, route, model_variant) bucket at 1m and 30s windows.
- Surface pulse-driven burn-rate alerts and an ensemble anomaly detector which can attach granular context (trace ids, example spans, top contributing features) to alerts.
- Implement a paging policy layer that uses pulse_score + customer-traffic signals to decide escalation level.

Non-goals: full redesign of existing SLI schema, replacing the current alerting backend, or shipping autoscaling changes as part of this ticket.

Why: Recent incidents (INC-2025-03-02) show regressions that only manifested when a particular sequence-length distribution hit the runtime kernels. Engineers currently lack precise, correlated evidence at alert time. The pulse aggregator will shrink time-to-context and reduce noisy pages by attaching ranked contributing signals and suggested mitigations.

Success criteria:
- Burn-rate alerts that include top-3 contributing signals and a link to 1 representative trace in <60s of alert creation.
- Page-on-call rate for false positives reduced by >=30% in canary cohort.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for latency regressions reduced by 20% in pilot services.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Extra metadata increases ingestion QPS and storage. We will use sampled-span enrichment (1% full traces + 100% lightweight telemetry-ids) to bound cost.
- Real-time scoring with <60s latency requires a stream processor; we prioritize a light-weight Flink/Streaming job over batch recompute to keep alerting timely.
- We accept slightly less-fine-grained attribution in exchange for faster scoring in the first rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry-id header propagated by service-side SDK and documented (X-RW-TID)
Ingest pipeline emits pulse_score and top_feature tags to telemetry-events-v2 kafka topic
Alerting rule created that ties burn-rate windows to pulse_score and includes trace link and contributing features
Paging policy accepts pulse_score input and can select escalation level based on traffic-weight and customer_impact tags
Canary rollout to 3 pilot services with synthetic probes and monitoring for false positives/negatives
comments: 2025-02-28 - Aisha Khan: Initial ticket created after post-incident review. Incident INC-2025-03-02 highlighted missing correlation between metrics and spans. Proposed lightweight telemetry-id approach to avoid full-trace ingestion costs.

2025-03-03 - Marco Varela: Spike finished. Validated header propagation in python/go SDKs and measured additional header add ~80 bytes; no high CPU impact. Chose 'X-RW-TID' as header name to avoid upstream rewrite conflicts.

2025-03-04 - Data Eng (review): Suggested using telemetry-events-v2 topic with compaction and topic-level retention to store per-minute pulse state instead of writing raw enriched spans to long-term storage. Agreed to compact to 7d then archive to long-term store.

2025-03-06 - Security review (notes): Header is opaque id; no PII added. Must ensure trace linking tools scrub user identifiers — added runbook check. Security sign-off pending automated test for id entropy.

2025-03-08 - Marco Varela: Implemented stream job prototype that computes pulse_score (ensemble: latency z-score, error-rate delta, queue-depth factor). Prototype pushed at PR runtime#5123. Scoring latency ~45s for 1m windows in dev cluster.

2025-03-10 - UX/Oncall review by Priya Desai: Request to include 'suggested mitigation' field with ranked steps (eg. rollback model variant, increase batch size on model pool) to reduce cognitive load during paging. We added a metadata slot for suggested_mitigation in the alert payload.

2025-03-11 - Canary plan updated: pilot services = model-serving-v2, routing-proxy, telemetry-ingest. Canary windows: 24h baseline, then 72h observation with synthetic probes every 60s. Fallback: disable pulse-driven pages if false positive rate >25% in first 24h.

2025-03-12 - QA: Integration tests added for header propagation and pulse_score emission. Observability E2E test simulates latency spike; alert created with trace link in ~38s. Next: finalize paging policy rule grammar and add operator UI knobs in console
